page: Amazon Web Services c7g.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture using Neoverse-V1 cores, this instance features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation model, operating at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7g.metal demonstrates strong multi-core performance and memory throughput. Multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench multi-core scores rank in the strong and top-tier categories respectively, highlighting the efficiency of the 64 dedicated physical cores. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with DDR5 memory achieving top-tier PassMark memory scores and strong read/write speeds on large blocks. Software compilation with Clang also registers in the top tier, making it highly effective for development pipelines. Conversely, single-core performance and low-parameter LLM text generation speeds are more modest, representing a tradeoff for workloads that rely on high single-threaded clock speeds or hardware acceleration.

The qualitative cost profile of the c7g.metal is defined by its high physical core density and the power efficiency of the ARM architecture. By eliminating hyperthreading and providing dedicated physical cores, it offers predictable execution dynamics for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of virtualized hypervisors. This server is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput web serving, redis database operations, and multi-threaded batch processing.
